Resolves #19450

A tab torn out of a dock opens its window at the dragged pane's size now, not the tab-header proxy's. `TearOut.onDockTearOutExit` measures the live pane's rendered rect at boundary exit, while the pane still lives in the source window, and carries it into the host's vessel request as `sourceRect`. `resolveVesselSize` is the engine-owned sizing helper hosts call: the source size by default, clamped to the display's available area with the title-bar delta off the height, the 320×240 floor surviving both clamps, and a host-pinned size when a staged composition sets one.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium: the Workstation pop-out e2e births a real native window and reads the born dims back against the pane's own live rect; the unit arms pin the payload, the measure-before-admission order and the helper's clamps, locally and in the unit tier) → L3 required (AC-3 asks for an e2e on the dock-popout or Workstation fixture). The e2e leg runs on this PR's CI. No residuals.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockTearOut.spec.mjs`: the exit payload carries the pane's rendered rect, measured before the host is asked; a dead measurement answers `null` and the gesture still admits |
| AC-2 | the same file, `resolveVesselSize`: source default, screen clamp with the title-bar delta, the floor under a degenerate rect and under a display smaller than the floor, the proxy then 480×360 fallback, a pin winning outright, and fractional rounding |
| AC-3 | `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNL.spec.mjs`: the pop-out test now asserts the born dims equal the pane's own rect clamped to the live display |
| AC-4 | `filmPace` pins `vesselSize` (320×240, the size the choreography was cut against); `executeTearOutStep` scopes the pin to the gesture and restores it afterwards; the film tours keep their footprint |

## Deltas from ticket
- Demo B adopts the helper as well: its `openTearOutVessel` carried the same floors, so the example stops shipping a stale copy of the replaced line. The engine workspace's own default `openTearOutVessel` adopts it too.
- The film's pin is the floor size (320×240), the size the choreography was tuned on; a source-sized vessel would cover targets the scene-3/4 drags cross.
- The measurement yields, never blocks: an unresolvable or throwing pane answers `null` and the host falls back to its proxy rect, so a collapsed rail tab keeps the floor behavior.
